Long table to one column per state

Source: R/group_compare.R
pivot_state_wide.Rd

Spreads feature of a long table (one row per id_col and state) into one column per state.

Usage

pivot_state_wide(
  df,
  id_col,
  feature,
  na = c("drop", "zero", "keep"),
  states = c("ctr", "ama")
)

Arguments

df

data.frame with the id_col column(s), a state column and feature.

id_col

Name(s) of the identifier column(s).

feature

Name of the value column.

na

"drop": remove rows with any NA; "zero": remove rows where both states are NA and set the remaining NA to 0; "keep": leave as is.

states

The two state names, c(reference, treatment).

Value

A data.frame with id_col and one column per state found in df$state (in order of first appearance), one row per identifier.

Examples

long <- data.frame(id = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 2),
                   state = rep(c("ctr", "ama"), each = 3),
                   usage = c(1, 2, NA, 2, 2, 5))
pivot_state_wide(long, "id", "usage")
#>   id ctr ama
#> 1  a   1   2
#> 2  b   2   2
pivot_state_wide(long, "id", "usage", na = "zero")
#>   id ctr ama
#> 1  a   1   2
#> 2  b   2   2
#> 3  c   0   5
